transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?
I came in because I’m having trouble stopping once I start eating. It’s like something switches on, and even while I’m thinking, “Dennis, stop already,” I just keep going.
Do you often eat much more rapidly than normal and continue eating until you feel uncomfortably full, even when you don’t mean to?
Yeah, I do. When it happens I eat really fast, like I’ll be standing at my desk between homework and a game, and I’m barely even tasting it. Then a few minutes later I realize the food’s just gone.
Does this eating behavior cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life, like affecting your work, social activities, or relationships?

Yeah, it does bother me. I’m still getting to class and robotics and all that, so it hasn’t totally thrown me off track. But sometimes the next morning I feel kind of sluggish or distracted, and I’ll spend way too much time worrying if my roommates noticed what happened. So… it’s more distressing than it is actually stopping me from doing things.
After eating like this, do you ever try to get rid of the calories by making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve worried about it after, but I haven’t made myself throw up or anything like that. I’m not sure about the exercise part… I don’t think I do a lot more than usual because of it.
How often does this kind of eating happen — like, how many times a week or month do you find yourself eating this way?

Since early in the semester, it’s been most weeks. Usually it’s one night a week, sometimes two if I’ve got deadlines or there’s a lot of food around the apartment. It’s been pretty steady like that for maybe three or four months.
Do you ever eat alone because you're worried others might notice or judge how much you're eating?

Yeah. If my roommates are around, I’ll usually eat a pretty normal amount in the kitchen. Then later I’ll take more food back to my room and eat it there, because I don’t want them seeing how much I’m actually eating.
After these episodes of eating, do you often feel guilty, ashamed, or down about yourself?

Yeah. I usually feel pretty embarrassed afterward, and kind of grossed out with myself. It bothers me because I’m normally pretty disciplined with school and robotics and stuff, so afterward it feels like I just wasn’t in control.
During these episodes, do you feel like you’re not in control of how much or what you’re eating, like you can’t stop even if you want to?

Yeah. That’s probably the main thing that made me come in. Once I start eating like that, it’s like some switch gets flipped, and I just keep going. Even while I’m thinking, like, “Dennis, stop already,” I still don’t.
Do these episodes usually happen when you're feeling down, stressed, or upset about something, or do they seem to come out of nowhere?
I’m not totally sure. I haven’t noticed one clear pattern. Sometimes I realize I was stressed afterward, but other times it feels like it just kind of happens.
Do you often eat a lot of food during these episodes even when you’re not really hungry?

I’m not totally sure. I don’t always notice whether I was actually hungry or not when it starts. Sometimes I just realize afterward that I ate a lot, but I can’t really say for sure it’s because I wasn’t hungry.
Do you feel a strong concern about your body shape or weight that bothers you a lot?
I don’t know if I’d say it’s a strong concern. I mean, I don’t love thinking about my weight, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether it bothers me that much.
Can you think of a recent time when you had one of these eating episodes — were you actually hungry before it started, or did you eat even though you weren’t?

I’m not sure. I can think of times recently where it happened, but I honestly don’t remember if I was hungry right before. It’s more like I noticed once I was already eating, or afterward, that it had gotten out of hand.
Do you feel a lot of distress or concern about these eating episodes, like they’re really bothering you or making you feel out of control?

Yeah, it really does bother me. What made me come in is that once I start eating like that, it feels like some switch gets flipped, and I just keep going even while part of me is thinking, “Dennis, stop already.” It feels out of my control.

Have you ever had episodes where you eat a very large amount of food in a short time, feel like you can’t stop yourself, and then feel really upset or guilty afterward, even though you don’t try to make up for it by vomiting or exercising more?

Yeah. The main thing is once I start, it feels like something kind of flips, and I just keep eating even though I’m thinking to myself, Dennis, stop. That’s what really scares me, that I don’t feel like I can stop it.
Can you recall if these episodes usually start when you're not actually physically hungry?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close enough attention to whether I’m actually hungry at the start. A lot of the time I only realize what’s happening once I’m already in it.
Can you think of a specific time when this happened — were you actually hungry before you started eating, or did you begin eating even though you weren’t hungry?

I honestly can’t think of a clear specific time where I noticed that. Like, I remember the eating getting out of hand, but I don’t really remember if I was actually hungry before it started or not. I guess I haven’t been paying attention to that part.
